title: Chouquettes (Pearl Sugar Choux Puffs)
summary: Little crisp choux puffs topped with crunchy pearl sugar, baked until deep golden and light as air.
equipment: piping bag with 1.2 cm plain nozzle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: the large, hard white nibs that do not melt in the oven

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan) and line the trays with baking paper.

steps.title: Panade
steps.text: bring the butter, water, milk, sugar and salt to a full boil, take off the heat and tip in all the flour. Beat hard, then return to low heat and keep beating 1-2 min until the paste forms a smooth ball and leaves a thin film on the pan. Cooking the flour paste dries it out so it can take more egg and puff higher.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: tip into the bowl and cool 5 min, stirring. Beat in the eggs a little at a time until the paste is glossy and falls from the spoon in a thick V; you may not need the last spoonful.

steps.title: Pipe
steps.text: pipe about 30 mounds 3 cm wide, 4 cm apart, and smooth any points with a wet fingertip. Beat the yolk with the milk and brush a thin coat on each mound without letting it drip onto the paper.

steps.title: Sugar
steps.text: press a generous pinch of pearl sugar onto the top and sides of each mound; it should look crowded, as the puffs double in size.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake 22-25 min, without opening the door for the first 15 min, until puffed, deep golden and light. Turn the oven off, prop the door ajar and leave 20 min so they dry and hold their shape, then cool on the rack. Steam inside lifts the puffs; opening the door too soon lets it escape and they sink.

tips: A common mistake is adding all the egg at once; add it slowly and stop when the paste falls in a V.
Pearl sugar keeps its shape in the oven; ordinary sugar melts, so do not swap it.
Bake one tray at a time on the middle shelf for even colour.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best within a few hours. Keep in a paper bag for up to 1 day, or freeze for 1 month and recrisp at 180 °C (160 °C fan) for 4-5 min.
